# ASCII Ocean Splash
中文 | English
A boot splash for DeepSeek Harness: pure black, one thin water line, a wordmark — then four characte
r-drawn sharks swim in and eat the wordmark letter by letter. When nothing is left, the screen holds
for three seconds and fades into the app.
The sharks are not hand-drawn here: the plugin bundles a copy of the ocean renderer from `dsh-ascii-
ocean` (MIT), so they look identical to the ocean background — same square cells, same glyph ramp (`
: ; t % S X 8 # @`), same spine-chain swimming.
## What it does
| Time | What happens |

| 0 – 1.7s | A 1px water line opens from the left; a faint far line appears at 32% height |
| 1.5 –

3.0s | `DEEPSEEK HARNESS` fades in |
| 0.3s / 1.5s | Two **routed** sharks enter from the screen edg

es (normal + 1.45×) |
| 3.0s / 3.6s | Two **free-swimming** sharks join, engine-driven, no fixed pat

h |
| ~10 – 12s | The routed pair cross the wordmark; every cell they cover is erased permanently |

| when coverage reaches 0 | Hold pure black for **3 seconds** |
| +3s | Fade to the app over 1.8s |
Press Esc or click anywhere to skip.
## Install
Requires DeepSeek Harness desktop 0.2.1 (tested) and a `desktop` profile.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or from a local checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then fully quit and reopen Harness — a splash only plays on a cold start. On Windows, closing the wi
ndow only minimizes to the tray; quit from the tray menu instead.
## Configuration
There is no settings page. Tune the constants at the top of `lib/boot.js`:
| Constant | Meaning |

| `WORD`, `TRACKING`, `FONT_SIZE` | The wordmark and its tracking |
| `HOLD` | How long the screen s

tays black after the wordmark is gone (ms) |
| `FADE` | Fade-out duration (ms) |
| `SPAWNS` | The fo

ur sharks: time, routed or free, direction, size |
| `renderer.settings.sharkColor` | Shark cell col

our (default `#4284FF`) |
| `renderer.settings.cellSize` | Cell size in px (default `6`) |
The 30fps frame cap and the 45-second watchdog are deliberate: the splash yields CPU to the app load
ing behind it, and can never leave you stuck on a black screen.
## How it works
- `index.js` runs on the host: it serves the two scripts and injects `<script src="/dsh-ocean-splash
/splash.js">` into `<head>` via `webserver/index-inject`, so the overlay exists before the first pai

nt.
- `lib/boot.js` builds a full-screen overlay, drives the timeline from the wall clock, erases th

e wordmark using the renderer's own shark grid, and fades out.
- `lib/ocean-renderer.js` is the bund
led ocean renderer. Two changes from upstream: the "keep the headline clear" steering force is disab

led (the sharks must cross the title), and the cruise speed is reduced for the splash.
- On Windows
the native window buttons are hidden only while the splash runs, by making the title-bar colour prob
e transparent through a CSS rule; the rule is removed when the splash ends.
The plugin never touches Harness's `window.__ModuleLoader__` — the bundled renderer loads through a
private `window.__DSH_OCEAN_LOADER__` hook, so client plugins keep loading normally.
## Known limitations

- Plays once per cold start; there is no replay command.
- Fixed ~16s timeline (10–12s of it is the

sharks crossing).
- Windows only for hiding the native window buttons; other platforms just skip tha

t step.
- The animation is wall-clock driven, so a suspended window resumes where the clock says it
The animation is wall-clock driven, so a suspended window resumes where the clock says it should be.
## Credits & license
MIT — see LICENSE.
`lib/ocean-renderer.js` is derived from the ocean renderer in `dsh-ascii-ocean` (MIT), which itself
ports the `ascii-sharks` demo by stackedlol. Its copyright notice is preserved by that MIT license;
the modifications made here are listed under "How it works".
